test_title: PYST 71: RRB Group D - GS (Held On: 29 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: When applying the sign conventions for spherical lenses to measure object and image distances, where are all measurements taken from?

options.text: The optical centre of the lens

solution:
The correct answer is __**The optical centre of the lens**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• For **spherical lenses**, we follow a set of sign conventions called the **New Cartesian Sign Convention** to measure distances.
 
• According to this convention, the **optical centre** (denoted by **O**) of the lens is taken as the **origin** of the coordinate system.
 
• The **principal axis** of the lens is taken as the **X-axis** (horizontal axis) of the coordinate system.
 
• All distances are measured from the **optical centre** of the lens. Distances measured in the direction of **incident light** (usually to the **right** of the optical centre) are taken as **positive**.
 
• Distances measured in the direction opposite to that of the **incident light** (usually to the **left** of the optical centre) are taken as **negative**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Object Distance (u)**:
 
 
• The **object** is always placed to the **left** of the lens.
 
• Since it is measured against the direction of incident light, the **object distance (u)** is always **negative** in both **convex** and **concave** lenses.
 
 
 
• **Image Distance (v)**:
 
 
• For a **real image**, which is formed on the **right side** of the lens, the image distance **v** is **positive**.
 
• For a **virtual image**, which is formed on the **left side** (the same side as the object), the image distance **v** is **negative**.
 
 
 
• **Focal Length (f)**:
 
 
• A **convex lens** (converging lens) has a **positive focal length** because its principal focus lies on the **right side**.
 
• A **concave lens** (diverging lens) has a **negative focal length** because its principal focus is considered to be on the **left side**.
 
 
 
• **Height of Object and Image (h and h')**:
 
 
• Distances measured **perpendicularly above** the principal axis are taken as **positive**. Thus, the **object height (h)** is usually **positive**.
 
• Distances measured **perpendicularly below** the principal axis are taken as **negative**. Therefore, the height of a **real and inverted image** is **negative**, while a **virtual and erect image** is **positive**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Lens Formula**: The relationship between the **object distance (u)**, **image distance (v)**, and **focal length (f)** is given by the formula: **1/v - 1/u = 1/f**. This formula is valid for all **spherical lenses** in all situations.
 
• **Magnification (m)**: The **linear magnification** produced by a lens is the ratio of the **height of the image** to the **height of the object**. It is expressed as **m = h'/h**. It is also related to distances as **m = v/u**.
 
• **Power of a Lens (P)**: The **power of a lens** is defined as the reciprocal of its **focal length** in **metres** (**P = 1/f**). The **SI unit** of power is **Dioptre (D)**. A **convex lens** has **positive power**, and a **concave lens** has **negative power**.
 
• **Comparison with Mirrors**: Unlike lenses where measurements start from the **optical centre**, in **spherical mirrors**, all measurements are taken from the **pole** of the mirror.
</ul
